Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	"""Winternitz one-time signature (W-OTS) for pqattest.
2	
3	Like the Lamport construction this is a **one-time** signature: a key pair
4	must sign at most one message. Each signing key is a set of hash chains; a
5	signature for a base-``B`` digit ``d`` reveals the value at chain step ``d``
6	and the public key holds the step ``B - 1`` endpoint. Only the standard
7	library is used. Keys and signatures have a deterministic, versioned v1
8	binary codec: :meth:`WOTSPrivateKey.to_bytes` /
9	:meth:`WOTSPrivateKey.from_bytes`, :meth:`WOTSPublicKey.to_bytes` /
10	:meth:`WOTSPublicKey.from_bytes`, and the stateless
11	:func:`wots_signature_to_bytes` / :func:`wots_signature_from_bytes`. The
12	private-key encoding contains the secret in the clear, so callers must store
13	it securely. :class:`WOTSOneTimeSigner` state can be persisted with a
14	versioned binary checkpoint (``checkpoint`` / ``from_checkpoint``); the blob
15	holds the private key in the clear and is integrity-protected only by a
16	SHA-256 checksum, so callers must store it securely.
17	"""
18	
19	from __future__ import annotations
20	
21	import hashlib
22	import secrets
23	import threading
24	from dataclasses import dataclass
25	from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable, Sequence
26	
27	from ._errors import KeyExhaustedError
28	from .auth import (
29	    _restore_auth_state,
30	    _validate_generation,
31	    _validate_key,
32	    auth_state_wrap,
33	)
34	
35	__all__ = [
36	    "ELEMENT_BYTES",
37	    "WOTSOneTimeSigner",
38	    "WOTSPrivateKey",
39	    "WOTSProof",
40	    "WOTSPublicKey",
41	    "wots_keygen",
42	    "wots_sign",
43	    "wots_signature_from_bytes",
44	    "wots_signature_to_bytes",
45	    "wots_verify",
46	]

48	ELEMENT_BYTES = 32
49	_DOMAIN = b"pqattest/wots/v1"
50	_ALLOWED_W = (4, 8)
51	
52	_CHECKPOINT_MAGIC = b"PQAWCP\0\0"
53	_CHECKPOINT_VERSION = 1
54	_CHECKPOINT_HEADER_BYTES = 8 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2
55	_CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES = 32
56	
57	_PRIVATE_KEY_MAGIC = b"PQAWPRV\0"
58	_PUBLIC_KEY_MAGIC = b"PQAWPUB\0"
59	_SIGNATURE_MAGIC = b"PQAWSIG\0"
60	_CODEC_VERSION = 1
61	_CODEC_HEADER_BYTES = 8 + 1 + 1 + 2
62	
63	_PROOF_MAGIC = b"PQAWPRF\0"
64	_PROOF_VERSION = 1
65	_PROOF_HEADER_BYTES = 8 + 1 + 4 + 4

67	
68	def _as_bytes(message: Any) -> bytes:
69	    if isinstance(message, bytes):
70	        return message
71	    if isinstance(message, bytearray):
72	        return bytes(message)
73	    if isinstance(message, str):
74	        return message.encode("utf-8")
75	    raise TypeError("message must be bytes, bytearray or str")
76	
77	
78	def _validate_w(w: Any) -> int:
79	    if isinstance(w, bool) or not isinstance(w, int) or w not in _ALLOWED_W:
80	        raise ValueError("w must be 4 or 8")
81	    return w
82	
83	
84	def _params(w: int) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
85	    """Return ``(B, l1, l2)``: base, message digit count, checksum digit count."""
86	    b = 1 << w
87	    l1 = 256 // w
88	    l2 = 1
89	    limit = l1 * (b - 1)
90	    while b ** l2 <= limit:
91	        l2 += 1
92	    return b, l1, l2
93	
94	
95	def _validate_elements(w: int, elements: Any) -> None:
96	    if not isinstance(elements, tuple):
97	        raise TypeError("elements must be a tuple of 32-byte values")
98	    _, l1, l2 = _params(w)
99	    if len(elements) != l1 + l2:
100	        raise ValueError(f"elements must contain exactly {l1 + l2} values for w={w}")
101	    for element in elements:
102	        if not isinstance(element, bytes) or len(element) != ELEMENT_BYTES:
103	            raise ValueError(f"every element must be exactly {ELEMENT_BYTES} bytes")
104	
105	
106	def _chain_count(w: int) -> int:
107	    _, l1, l2 = _params(w)
108	    return l1 + l2
109	
110	
111	def _encode_v1(magic: bytes, w: int, elements: tuple[bytes, ...]) -> bytes:
112	    """Shared v1 layout: magic, version, ``w``, element count, elements."""
113	    return (
114	        magic
115	        + bytes((_CODEC_VERSION, w))
116	        + len(elements).to_bytes(2, "big")
117	        + b"".join(elements)
118	    )
119

121	def _decode_v1(data: Any, magic: bytes, name: str) -> tuple[int, tuple[bytes, ...]]:
122	    """Parse a v1 blob into ``(w, elements)``; ``name`` labels error messages."""
123	    if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
124	        raise TypeError(f"{name} data must be bytes or bytearray")
125	    data = bytes(data)
126	    if len(data) < _CODEC_HEADER_BYTES:
127	        raise ValueError(f"{name} encoding is truncated")
128	    if data[:8] != magic:
129	        raise ValueError(f"bad {name} magic")
130	    if data[8] != _CODEC_VERSION:
131	        raise ValueError(f"unsupported {name} version: {data[8]}")
132	    w = _validate_w(data[9])
133	    element_count = int.from_bytes(data[10:12], "big")
134	    chains = _chain_count(w)
135	    if element_count != chains:
136	        raise ValueError("element count does not match the chain count for w")
137	    expected = _CODEC_HEADER_BYTES + element_count * ELEMENT_BYTES
138	    if len(data) < expected:
139	        raise ValueError(f"{name} encoding is truncated")
140	    if len(data) > expected:
141	        raise ValueError(f"trailing data after the {name} encoding")
142	    elements = tuple(
143	        data[_CODEC_HEADER_BYTES + i * ELEMENT_BYTES : _CODEC_HEADER_BYTES + (i + 1) * ELEMENT_BYTES]
144	        for i in range(element_count)
145	    )
146	    return w, elements
147	
148	
149	def _key_to_bytes(key: Any, key_type: type, magic: bytes, name: str) -> bytes:
150	    if not isinstance(key, key_type):
151	        raise TypeError(f"to_bytes must be called on a {key_type.__name__}")
152	    try:
153	        w = _validate_w(key.w)
154	        _validate_elements(w, key.elements)
155	    except TypeError as exc:
156	        raise ValueError(f"corrupted {name}: {exc}") from exc
157	    return _encode_v1(magic, w, key.elements)

160	@dataclass(frozen=True)
161	class WOTSPrivateKey:
162	    """Frozen W-OTS private key.
163	
164	    ``elements`` holds the random step-0 start value of every chain: the
165	    ``l1`` message chains followed by the ``l2`` checksum chains.
166	    """
167	
168	    w: int
169	    elements: tuple[bytes, ...]
170	
171	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
172	        w = _validate_w(self.w)
173	        _validate_elements(w, self.elements)
174	
175	    @property
176	    def length(self) -> int:
177	        """Number of chains (and signature elements): ``l1 + l2``."""
178	        return len(self.elements)
179	
180	    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes:
181	        """Serialise to the versioned v1 wire format as ``bytes``.
182	
183	        The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAWPRV\\0"``; one byte each for
184	        the version (1) and ``w``; the element count as 2 big-endian bytes
185	        (67 for ``w=4``, 34 for ``w=8``); then every private element in chain
186	        order, 32 bytes each. Encoding is deterministic: the same key always
187	        produces the same bytes. Fields corrupted by bypassing the frozen
188	        constructor raise ``ValueError`` instead of producing a malformed
189	        encoding. The blob contains the private key in the clear — store it
190	        as a secret.
191	        """
192	        return _key_to_bytes(self, WOTSPrivateKey, _PRIVATE_KEY_MAGIC, "private key")

194	    @classmethod
195	    def from_bytes(cls, data: Any) -> "WOTSPrivateKey":
196	        """Parse ``to_bytes()`` output back into a :class:`WOTSPrivateKey`.
197	
198	        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
199	        ``TypeError``. A bad magic, an unknown version, an invalid ``w``, an
200	        element count that does not match the chain count for ``w``,
201	        truncation or trailing data raises ``ValueError`` and no instance is
202	        returned. The restored key is equal by value to the original.
203	        """
204	        w, elements = _decode_v1(data, _PRIVATE_KEY_MAGIC, "private key")
205	        return cls(w=w, elements=elements)

208	@dataclass(frozen=True)
209	class WOTSPublicKey:
210	    """Frozen W-OTS public key: the step ``B - 1`` endpoint of every chain."""
211	
212	    w: int
213	    elements: tuple[bytes, ...]
214	
215	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
216	        w = _validate_w(self.w)
217	        _validate_elements(w, self.elements)
218	
219	    @property
220	    def length(self) -> int:
221	        """Number of chains (and signature elements): ``l1 + l2``."""
222	        return len(self.elements)
223	
224	    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes:
225	        """Serialise to the versioned v1 wire format as ``bytes``.
226	
227	        The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAWPUB\\0"``; one byte each for
228	        the version (1) and ``w``; the element count as 2 big-endian bytes
229	        (67 for ``w=4``, 34 for ``w=8``); then every public element in chain
230	        order, 32 bytes each. Encoding is deterministic: the same key always
231	        produces the same bytes. Fields corrupted by bypassing the frozen
232	        constructor raise ``ValueError`` instead of producing a malformed
233	        encoding.
234	        """
235	        return _key_to_bytes(self, WOTSPublicKey, _PUBLIC_KEY_MAGIC, "public key")
236	
237	    @classmethod
238	    def from_bytes(cls, data: Any) -> "WOTSPublicKey":
239	        """Parse ``to_bytes()`` output back into a :class:`WOTSPublicKey`.
240	
241	        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
242	        ``TypeError``. A bad magic, an unknown version, an invalid ``w``, an
243	        element count that does not match the chain count for ``w``,
244	        truncation or trailing data raises ``ValueError`` and no instance is
245	        returned. The restored key is equal by value to the original.

251	def _chain_step(value: bytes) -> bytes:
252	    return hashlib.sha256(_DOMAIN + value).digest()
253	
254	
255	def _chain_walk(value: bytes, steps: int) -> bytes:
256	    for _ in range(steps):
257	        value = _chain_step(value)
258	    return value

261	def _message_digits(digest: bytes, w: int, b: int, l1: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
262	    """Split a 256-bit digest into ``l1`` base-``B`` digits, big endian."""
263	    value = int.from_bytes(digest, "big")
264	    return tuple((value >> (256 - w * (i + 1))) & (b - 1) for i in range(l1))
265	
266	
267	def _checksum_digits(
268	    message_digits: Iterable[int], w: int, b: int, l2: int
269	) -> tuple[int, ...]:
270	    """``sum(B - 1 - d)`` as exactly ``l2`` base-``B`` digits, leading zeros kept."""
271	    checksum = sum(b - 1 - digit for digit in message_digits)
272	    return tuple((checksum >> (w * (l2 - 1 - i))) & (b - 1) for i in range(l2))
273

275	def _signing_digits(message: Any, w: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
276	    b, l1, l2 = _params(w)
277	    digest = hashlib.sha256(_as_bytes(message)).digest()
278	    message_part = _message_digits(digest, w, b, l1)
279	    return message_part + _checksum_digits(message_part, w, b, l2)

282	class WOTSOneTimeSigner:
283	    """Thread-safe, single-use wrapper around a :class:`WOTSPrivateKey`.
284	
285	    The first :meth:`sign` call returns the ordinary :func:`wots_sign`
286	    signature and marks the key as used; every later call raises
287	    :class:`~pqattest.KeyExhaustedError`. The guard is per instance and per
288	    process — copying the private key, calling the stateless :func:`wots_sign`
289	    directly or reusing the key in another process is the caller's
290	    responsibility. State can be persisted with :meth:`checkpoint` and
291	    restored in another process with :meth:`from_checkpoint`; the checkpoint
292	    contains the private key in the clear and is protected only by a SHA-256
293	    checksum against accidental corruption, so callers must store it securely.
294	    :meth:`sign_with_checkpoint` pairs the single signature with the
295	    post-sign checkpoint in one atomic call.
296	    """
297	
298	    __slots__ = ("_lock", "_private_key", "_public_key", "_used")
299	
300	    def __init__(self, private_key: WOTSPrivateKey) -> None:
301	        if not isinstance(private_key, WOTSPrivateKey):
302	            raise TypeError("private_key must be a WOTSPrivateKey")
303	        self._restore_state(private_key, self._public_key_from(private_key), False)
304	
305	    @staticmethod
306	    def _public_key_from(private_key: WOTSPrivateKey) -> WOTSPublicKey:
307	        b = 1 << private_key.w
308	        return WOTSPublicKey(
309	            w=private_key.w,
310	            elements=tuple(
311	                _chain_walk(start, b - 1) for start in private_key.elements
312	            ),
313	        )
314	
315	    def _restore_state(
316	        self,
317	        private_key: WOTSPrivateKey,
318	        public_key: WOTSPublicKey,
319	        used: bool,
320	    ) -> None:
321	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
322	        self._private_key = private_key
323	        self._public_key = public_key
324	        self._used = used
325	
326	    @property
327	    def public_key(self) -> WOTSPublicKey:
328	        """Public key derived from the wrapped private key (read-only)."""
329	        return self._public_key
330	
331	    @property
332	    def used(self) -> bool:
333	        """``True`` once a signature has been produced (read-only)."""
334	        return self._used
335	
336	    def sign(self, message: Any) -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
337	        """Sign once.
338	
339	        Behaves exactly like :func:`wots_sign` on the first successful call,
340	        accepting ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str``; an unsupported message type
341	        raises the same ``TypeError`` that :func:`wots_sign` raises without
342	        consuming the key. Any later call raises
343	        :class:`~pqattest.KeyExhaustedError`. Concurrent calls are serialised
344	        on one lock so that at most one succeeds and every loser raises
345	        :class:`~pqattest.KeyExhaustedError`.
346	        """
347	        with self._lock:
348	            if self._used:
349	                raise KeyExhaustedError("this one-time signing key has already been used")
350	            signature = wots_sign(message, self._private_key)
351	            self._used = True
352	            return signature
353	
354	    def _checkpoint_bytes(self) -> bytes:
355	        """Serialise the signer state; the caller holds the lock."""
356	        body = (
357	            _CHECKPOINT_MAGIC
358	            + bytes((_CHECKPOINT_VERSION, self._private_key.w, int(self._used)))
359	            + len(self._private_key.elements).to_bytes(2, "big")
360	            + b"".join(self._private_key.elements)
361	        )
362	        return body + hashlib.sha256(body).digest()
363	
364	    def checkpoint(self) -> bytes:
365	        """Serialise the signer state (private key plus ``used``) to ``bytes``.
366	
367	        The v1 layout is: the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAWCP\\0\\0"``; one byte each
368	        for the version (1), ``w`` and ``used`` (0 or 1); the element count as
369	        2 big-endian bytes (67 for ``w=4``, 34 for ``w=8``); every private key
370	        element in chain order (32 bytes each); and finally the SHA-256 of all
371	        preceding content. Encoding is deterministic: the same state always
372	        produces the same bytes.

375	        reflects the state either immediately before or immediately after an
376	        in-flight :meth:`sign`, never part-way through one. The blob contains
377	        the private key in the clear and the trailing hash only detects
378	        accidental corruption — store it as a secret.
379	        """
380	        with self._lock:
381	            return self._checkpoint_bytes()

383	    def sign_with_checkpoint(self, message: Any) -> tuple[tuple[bytes, ...], bytes]:

388	        post-sign ``used=True`` state, all under the signing lock — but
389	        instead of the signature alone it returns ``(signature,

396	        halves in one call keeps the signature and the state it advanced
397	        to together, so a caller can never match a signature against a
398	        checkpoint taken at the wrong point under concurrency.

401	        key, and an already used instance raises

408	        accidental corruption — it offers no authentication, encryption or

410	        rollback protection remain the caller's responsibility.

472	    @classmethod
473	    def from_checkpoint(cls, data: Any) -> "WOTSOneTimeSigner":
474	        """Restore a signer from ``checkpoint()`` output without randomness.
475	
476	        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
477	        ``TypeError``. A bad magic, version, ``w``, ``used`` flag, element
478	        count, length, truncation, trailing data or checksum mismatch raises
479	        ``ValueError`` and no instance is returned. The private key and the
480	        public key rebuilt from it are identical to the original's, so a
481	        restored unused signer still allows exactly one signature and a
482	        checkpoint taken after signing restores a signer whose every call
483	        raises :class:`~pqattest.KeyExhaustedError`.
484	        """
485	        if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
486	            raise TypeError("checkpoint data must be bytes or bytearray")
487	        data = bytes(data)
488	        header = _CHECKPOINT_HEADER_BYTES
489	        if len(data) < header + _CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES:
490	            raise ValueError("checkpoint is too short")
491	        body, checksum = data[:-_CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES], data[-_CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES:]
492	        if body[:8] != _CHECKPOINT_MAGIC:
493	            raise ValueError("bad checkpoint magic")
494	        if body[8] != _CHECKPOINT_VERSION:
495	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported checkpoint version: {body[8]}")
496	        w = _validate_w(body[9])
497	        used_byte = body[10]
498	        if used_byte not in (0, 1):
499	            raise ValueError("used flag must be 0 or 1")
500	        element_count = int.from_bytes(body[11:13], "big")
501	        _, l1, l2 = _params(w)
502	        chains = l1 + l2
503	        if element_count != chains:
504	            raise ValueError("element count does not match the chain count for w")
505	        if len(body) != header + element_count * ELEMENT_BYTES:
506	            raise ValueError("checkpoint length does not match the element count")
507	        if hashlib.sha256(body).digest() != checksum:
508	            raise ValueError("checkpoint checksum mismatch")
509	        elements = tuple(
510	            body[header + i * ELEMENT_BYTES : header + (i + 1) * ELEMENT_BYTES]
511	            for i in range(element_count)
512	        )
513	        private_key = WOTSPrivateKey(w=w, elements=elements)
514	        signer = cls.__new__(cls)
515	        signer._restore_state(
516	            private_key, cls._public_key_from(private_key), bool(used_byte)
517	        )
518	        return signer
519	
520	    @classmethod
521	    def from_auth_state(
522	        cls, data: Any, *, key: Any, min_generation: Any = None, claim: Any
523	    ) -> tuple["WOTSOneTimeSigner", int]:
524	        """Restore a signer from a v2 ``"wots"`` envelope and claim it once.
525	
526	        Combines v2 verification, the generation floor and the v1 checkpoint
527	        restore in one call without drawing randomness, and — only once
528	        everything has succeeded — performs the external monotonic claim so a
529	        caller can never accept a restored key without also claiming its
530	        generation. Only an envelope produced by :func:`auth_state_wrap` with
531	        ``scheme="wots"`` is accepted; no new format is introduced.
532	        ``key``, ``min_generation`` and ``claim`` are keyword-only. Returns
533	        ``(signer, generation)``: the restored :class:`WOTSOneTimeSigner`
534	        (equal to :meth:`from_checkpoint` on the embedded payload) and the
535	        non-negative uint64 generation carried in the envelope.
536	
537	        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; ``key`` must be a
538	        non-empty ``bytes``/``bytearray`` shared secret; ``min_generation``
539	        must be ``None`` or a non-boolean integer in ``0 .. 2**64 - 1``;
540	        ``claim`` must be callable. A wrong type (including a boolean floor or
541	        a non-callable claim) raises ``TypeError``. The v2 HMAC tag is
542	        verified first with :func:`hmac.compare_digest`; the envelope scheme
543	        is then fixed to ``"wots"``, the payload magic checked and the
544	        generation floor applied; only afterwards is the untouched payload
545	        handed to :meth:`from_checkpoint`. Once the checkpoint is restored,
546	        ``claim`` is called exactly once with the single token
547	        ``("wots", generation)``; the restore succeeds only when that call
548	        returns ``True`` (compared by identity), and any exception it raises
549	        propagates untouched. An empty key, a bad tag or envelope, a non-wots
550	        scheme (including a v1 envelope), a generation below the floor, an
551	        invalid checkpoint, or a claim that is not ``True`` raises
552	        ``ValueError`` and the callback is never invoked on such a failure.
553	        """
554	        return _restore_auth_state(
555	            "wots",
556	            data,
557	            key=key,
558	            min_generation=min_generation,
559	            claim=claim,
560	            restore=cls.from_checkpoint,
561	        )

564	def wots_keygen(
565	    *,
566	    w: int = 4,
567	    token_bytes: Callable[[int], bytes] = secrets.token_bytes,
568	) -> tuple[WOTSPrivateKey, WOTSPublicKey]:
569	    """Generate a fresh W-OTS key pair.
570	
571	    ``w`` selects the Winternitz parameter and must be 4 or 8. Every chain
572	    starts at a random 32-byte value from ``token_bytes``; the public key
573	    stores each chain's step ``B - 1`` endpoint.
574	    """
575	    w = _validate_w(w)
576	    b, l1, l2 = _params(w)
577	    starts = tuple(bytes(token_bytes(ELEMENT_BYTES)) for _ in range(l1 + l2))
578	    for start in starts:
579	        if len(start) != ELEMENT_BYTES:
580	            raise ValueError(f"token_bytes must return {ELEMENT_BYTES} bytes")
581	    private_key = WOTSPrivateKey(w=w, elements=starts)
582	    endpoints = tuple(_chain_walk(start, b - 1) for start in starts)
583	    return private_key, WOTSPublicKey(w=w, elements=endpoints)
584

586	def wots_sign(message: Any, private_key: WOTSPrivateKey) -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
587	    """Sign ``message``: for each digit ``d`` reveal chain value at step ``d``.
588	
589	    Message digits come first, followed by the fixed-width checksum digits.
590	    """
591	    if not isinstance(private_key, WOTSPrivateKey):
592	        raise TypeError("private_key must be a WOTSPrivateKey")
593	    digits = _signing_digits(message, private_key.w)
594	    return tuple(
595	        _chain_walk(private_key.elements[i], digit)
596	        for i, digit in enumerate(digits)
597	    )
598

600	def wots_verify(
601	    message: Any, signature: Sequence[Any], public_key: WOTSPublicKey
602	) -> bool:
603	    """Complete the remaining chain steps and compare every public endpoint.
604	
605	    Returns ``False`` for any structural, parameter or content mismatch; only
606	    a wrong key *type* raises ``TypeError``.
607	    """
608	    if not isinstance(public_key, WOTSPublicKey):
609	        raise TypeError("public_key must be a WOTSPublicKey")
610	    w = public_key.w
611	    b, l1, l2 = _params(w)
612	    length = l1 + l2
613	
614	    try:
615	        parts = tuple(bytes(part) for part in signature)
616	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
617	        return False
618	    if len(parts) != length or len(public_key.elements) != length:
619	        return False
620	    if any(len(part) != ELEMENT_BYTES for part in parts):
621	        return False
622	
623	    try:
624	        digits = _signing_digits(message, w)
625	    except TypeError:
626	        return False
627	    for i, digit in enumerate(digits):
628	        endpoint = _chain_walk(parts[i], b - 1 - digit)
629	        if endpoint != public_key.elements[i]:
630	            return False
631	    return True

634	def wots_signature_to_bytes(signature: Any, *, w: int) -> bytes:
635	    """Serialise a stateless W-OTS signature to the versioned v1 wire format.
636	
637	    ``signature`` must be a ``tuple`` whose members are all ``bytes`` — the
638	    shape :func:`wots_sign` returns; anything else raises ``TypeError``.
639	    ``w`` is keyword-only and must be 4 or 8 (``ValueError`` otherwise); the
640	    signature must contain exactly the chain count for ``w`` (67 or 34
641	    elements) and every element must be exactly 32 bytes, else ``ValueError``.
642	
643	    The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAWSIG\\0"``; one byte each for the
644	    version (1) and ``w``; the element count as 2 big-endian bytes; then every
645	    signature element in chain order, 32 bytes each. Encoding is
646	    deterministic: the same signature and ``w`` always produce the same
647	    bytes.
648	    """
649	    if not isinstance(signature, tuple):
650	        raise TypeError("signature must be a tuple of 32-byte values")
651	    for element in signature:
652	        if not isinstance(element, bytes):
653	            raise TypeError("every signature element must be bytes")
654	    w = _validate_w(w)
655	    chains = _chain_count(w)
656	    if len(signature) != chains:
657	        raise ValueError(f"signature must contain exactly {chains} elements for w={w}")
658	    for element in signature:
659	        if len(element) != ELEMENT_BYTES:
660	            raise ValueError(f"every signature element must be exactly {ELEMENT_BYTES} bytes")
661	    return _encode_v1(_SIGNATURE_MAGIC, w, signature)
662	
663	
664	def wots_signature_from_bytes(data: Any) -> tuple[int, tuple[bytes, ...]]:
665	    """Parse ``wots_signature_to_bytes()`` output back into ``(w, elements)``.
666	
667	    ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
668	    ``TypeError``. A bad magic, an unknown version, an invalid ``w``, an
669	    element count that does not match the chain count for ``w``, truncation
670	    or trailing data raises ``ValueError``. The returned ``elements`` are an
671	    immutable ``tuple`` of 32-byte ``bytes`` in the original chain order,
672	    ready for :func:`wots_verify`.
673	    """
674	    return _decode_v1(data, _SIGNATURE_MAGIC, "signature")
675	
676	
677	def _wots_signature_matches_key(signature: Any, public_key: Any) -> bool:
678	    """Non-raising parameter/count check for a W-OTS proof pair."""
679	    if not isinstance(public_key, WOTSPublicKey):
680	        return False
681	    try:
682	        w = _validate_w(public_key.w)
683	    except (ValueError, AttributeError):
684	        return False
685	    if not isinstance(signature, tuple) or len(signature) != _chain_count(w):
686	        return False
687	    return all(
688	        isinstance(element, bytes) and len(element) == ELEMENT_BYTES
689	        for element in signature
690	    )

693	@dataclass(frozen=True)
694	class WOTSProof:
695	    """Frozen, self-contained bundle of one W-OTS public key and one signature.
696	
697	    Unlike a bare signature tuple (whose wire encoding needs ``w`` supplied
698	    separately), a proof carries the :class:`WOTSPublicKey` that constrains
699	    its signature, so it can be transported on its own as a single byte block
700	    and verified with :meth:`verify`. The proof stores no message and is a
701	    pure serialisation container: it offers neither authentication nor
702	    encryption of the wrapper itself, draws no randomness, generates
703	    no keys and keeps no state.
704	    """
705	
706	    public_key: WOTSPublicKey
707	    signature: tuple[bytes, ...]
708	
709	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
710	        if not isinstance(self.public_key, WOTSPublicKey):
711	            raise TypeError("public_key must be a WOTSPublicKey")
712	        if not isinstance(self.signature, tuple):
713	            raise TypeError("signature must be a tuple of 32-byte values")
714	        if not all(isinstance(element, bytes) for element in self.signature):
715	            raise TypeError("every signature element must be bytes")
716	        if not _wots_signature_matches_key(self.signature, self.public_key):
717	            raise ValueError(
718	                "signature chain count or elements do not match the public key"
719	            )
720	
721	    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes:
722	        """Serialise to the versioned v1 proof wire format as ``bytes``.
723	
724	        The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQAWPRF\\0"``; one version byte
725	        (1); the public-key and signature lengths as 4 big-endian bytes each;
726	        then the existing v1 encodings of the public key and of the signature
727	        constrained by that key, in that order (the inner encodings are
728	        reused unchanged). Encoding is deterministic: the same proof always
729	        produces the same bytes. A field corrupted by bypassing the frozen
730	        constructor raises ``ValueError`` instead of producing malformed
731	        bytes.
732	        """
733	        if not isinstance(self, WOTSProof):
734	            raise TypeError("to_bytes must be called on a WOTSProof")
735	        try:
736	            key_bytes = self.public_key.to_bytes()
737	            signature_bytes = wots_signature_to_bytes(
738	                self.signature, w=self.public_key.w
739	            )
740	        except (TypeError, AttributeError) as exc:
741	            raise ValueError(f"corrupted proof field: {exc}") from exc
742	        return (
743	            _PROOF_MAGIC
744	            + bytes((_PROOF_VERSION,))
745	            + len(key_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big")
746	            + len(signature_bytes).to_bytes(4, "big")
747	            + key_bytes
748	            + signature_bytes
749	        )
750	
751	    @classmethod
752	    def from_bytes(cls, data: Any) -> "WOTSProof":
753	        """Parse ``to_bytes()`` output back into a :class:`WOTSProof`.
754	
755	        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
756	        ``TypeError``. The embedded public key is recovered first and then
757	        constrains the signature. A bad magic, an unknown version, a length
758	        field that is out of bounds or disagrees with the actual content,
759	        truncation, trailing data, an invalid nested encoding, or a signature
760	        inconsistent with the key (wrong ``w`` or chain count) raises
761	        ``ValueError`` and no half-valid object is returned.
762	        """
763	        if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
764	            raise TypeError("proof data must be bytes or bytearray")
765	        data = bytes(data)
766	        if len(data) < _PROOF_HEADER_BYTES:
767	            raise ValueError("proof encoding is truncated")
768	        if data[:8] != _PROOF_MAGIC:
769	            raise ValueError("bad proof magic")
770	        if data[8] != _PROOF_VERSION:
771	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported proof version: {data[8]}")
772	        key_length = int.from_bytes(data[9:13], "big")
773	        signature_length = int.from_bytes(data[13:17], "big")
774	        key_end = _PROOF_HEADER_BYTES + key_length
775	        signature_end = key_end + signature_length
776	        if key_length == 0 or signature_length == 0:
777	            raise ValueError("a length field must not be zero")
778	        if key_end > len(data) or signature_end > len(data):
779	            raise ValueError("proof encoding is truncated")
780	        if signature_end < len(data):
781	            raise ValueError("trailing data after the proof encoding")
782	        public_key = WOTSPublicKey.from_bytes(data[_PROOF_HEADER_BYTES:key_end])
783	        w, signature = wots_signature_from_bytes(data[key_end:signature_end])
784	        if w != public_key.w:
785	            raise ValueError("signature w does not match the public key")
786	        return cls(public_key=public_key, signature=signature)
787	
788	    def verify(self, message: Any) -> bool:
789	        """Verify the embedded signature against the embedded public key.
790	
791	        Accepts ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str`` exactly like
792	        :func:`wots_verify`, to which this call delegates; it returns
793	        ``True`` only for the message that was actually signed. Any change to
794	        the message, public key or signature, an illegal message type, or
795	        fields corrupted by bypassing the frozen constructor returns
796	        ``False`` instead of raising. The proof itself carries no message and
797	        cannot authenticate its own origin.
798	        """
799	        try:
800	            return wots_verify(message, self.signature, self.public_key)
801	        except Exception:
802	            return False
803	
804	    def verify_bound(self, message: Any, *, public_key: Any) -> bool:
805	        """Verify the signature and bind the proof to an expected public key.
806	
807	        First requires ``public_key`` to equal the public key embedded in
808	        the proof, compared by value, then runs the exact verification of
809	        :meth:`verify` — ``message`` is checked against the embedded
810	        signature with :func:`wots_verify`, accepting
811	        ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str`` (a ``str`` is encoded as UTF-8).
812	        No wire format changes, no new objects, no randomness and no state
813	        are involved.
814	
815	        ``public_key`` must be a :class:`WOTSPublicKey`; any other type
816	        raises ``TypeError``. Missing or mistyped embedded fields
817	        (including values corrupted by bypassing the frozen constructor),
818	        any public-key value mismatch, and any message or signature
819	        mismatch return ``False`` without leaking any other exception.
820	        """
821	        if not isinstance(public_key, WOTSPublicKey):
822	            raise TypeError("public_key must be a WOTSPublicKey")
823	        try:
824	            embedded_key = self.public_key
825	            signature = self.signature
826	            if not isinstance(embedded_key, WOTSPublicKey):
827	                return False
828	            if embedded_key != public_key:
829	                return False
830	            return wots_verify(message, signature, embedded_key)
831	        except Exception:
832	            # A bypass-constructed proof may carry arbitrary field objects
833	            # whose access or comparison raises anything; the bound check
834	            # reports every such malformed structure as ``False``. External
835	            # argument type errors were raised before this block.
836	            return False
